result.body:
## Summary

- The drift between `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` (published by CI) and
  `src/lamp_the_djinn/devcontainer/Dockerfile` (the packaged local-build
  fallback) is mostly **deliberate**: Docker CLI, the pinned global Playwright
  CLI, the extra ipset sudoers lines, and the OCI build-metadata labels are
  each tied to a real difference in what the two images are for (see the
  comments in each file, `src/lamp_the_djinn/parser.py`'s `--volume` flag, and
  `src/lamp_the_djinn/mount_ownership.py`'s sudoers-allowlist note). One piece
  was **accidental**: `known_hosts` was `chmod 644` in the devcontainer copy
  and `600` in the packaged one, with no rationale anywhere for the weaker
  permission. Fixed to `600` in both.
- Since the drift is mostly deliberate, the parity check
  (`tests/integration/dockerfile_parity_test.py`) pins the *shared*
  invariants — base image version, tool version pins, the apt/pnpm/Claude
  Code/pi install steps, the firewall-script `COPY`s, the `ENV` block — using
  `dockerfile-parse` rather than a byte diff, so it isn't tripped by the
  legitimate differences.
- Hadolint only ever ran against `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, so the shipped
  Dockerfile was never linted. Its ignore config
  (`.devcontainer/.hadolint.yaml`) was *also* silently unused: hadolint only
  auto-discovers `.hadolint.yaml` from the process's cwd, not relative to the
  file being linted, so in CI (cwd = repo root) it was never picked up.
  Moved the config to the repo root (`.hadolint.yaml`) so it covers both
  files with no `--config` flag needed, and lint both in
  `.github/workflows/lint-dockerfile.yml`.
- Checked what hadolint reports on both files today before deciding on
  `continue-on-error`: with the config-discovery bug fixed, both files hit
  DL3008/DL3059 (already ignored, rationale documented in `.hadolint.yaml`)
  and DL4006 (missing `SHELL -o pipefail` before a `RUN` with a pipe — worse
  on the packaged file, which has two pipe-using `RUN`s). Fixed DL4006 for
  real on both files (`SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c", "-o", "pipefail"]`, verified
  with a real `docker build` that it fails a pipe correctly) instead of
  adding it to the ignore list, so the job now blocks the PR on any finding
  rather than staying advisory.

## Issue reconciliation

#103 and #88 cover the same ground: #103 (hadolint never lints the shipped
Dockerfile) is a narrower duplicate of #88 (the two Dockerfiles have drifted;
add a parity check), filed a few hours later without noticing #88 already
existed. Closing #103 as a duplicate with a comment pointing here.

Fixes #88

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest -m unit` — 150 passed
- [x] `uv run pytest -m integration` — 37 passed (includes the new parity test)
- [x] `uvx ruff check .` / `uvx ruff format --check .`
- [x] `uvx mypy src/lamp_the_djinn`
- [x] `pnpm dlx testing-conventions@0.0.120` — `unit lint`, `unit
      one-function-per-file`, `unit colocated-test`, `integration lint`,
      `unit mutation` (no mutatable changed lines), `packaging` (built wheel,
      no stray test files)
- [x] `uvx testing-conventions e2e attest 'uv run pytest tests/e2e/workspace_test.py -m e2e'`
      — 10 passed, 2 skipped (receipt committed)
- [x] `hadolint` on both Dockerfiles — clean (exit 0)
- [x] `actionlint` on `.github/workflows/lint-dockerfile.yml` — clean

+"""
+Integration tests pinning the shared invariants between the two cage Dockerfiles.
+
+`.devcontainer/Dockerfile` is what CI builds and publishes to ghcr.io -- the
+image `ltd` pulls by default. `src/lamp_the_djinn/devcontainer/Dockerfile` is
+the copy embedded in the wheel, used as the local-build fallback when the pull
+fails or `--build` is passed. Both run arbitrary agent workloads, so the tool
+versions and base image they hand an agent must not drift apart by accident.
+
+They also legitimately differ: only the packaged copy installs the Docker CLI
+and a pinned global Playwright CLI (a devcontainer.json used purely to develop
+this repo mounts no docker socket and needs neither), and only the published
+image carries OCI build-metadata labels. This test does not assert byte
+equality -- see the comments on each check for what is and isn't shared.
+
+The real, controlled collaborator is the host filesystem: dockerfile_parse
+reads the two files as they exist in this checkout. Nothing first-party is
+mocked.
+"""
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+from dockerfile_parse import DockerfileParser
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+DEVCONTAINER_DOCKERFILE = REPO_ROOT / ".devcontainer" / "Dockerfile"
+PACKAGED_DOCKERFILE = REPO_ROOT / "src" / "lamp_the_djinn" / "devcontainer" / "Dockerfile"
+
+# Bumping one of these in only one image is exactly the drift this test exists
+# to catch (see issue #88: PRs #79 and #85 each had to hand-patch both files).
+SHARED_ARG_DEFAULTS = ("CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION", "PI_VERSION", "GIT_DELTA_VERSION", "PNPM_VERSION")
+
+# RUN instructions that must be byte-identical between the two images,
+# identified by a substring unique to each.
+SHARED_RUN_NEEDLES = (
+    "apt-get install",
+    "pnpm@",
+    "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@",
+    "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@",
+    "known_hosts",
+)
+
+
+def _run_containing(dfp: DockerfileParser, needle: str) -> str:
+    matches = [s["value"] for s in dfp.structure if s["instruction"] == "RUN" and needle in s["value"]]
+    assert len(matches) == 1, f"expected exactly one RUN instruction containing {needle!r}, found {len(matches)}"
+    return matches[0]
+
+
+def _copy_instructions(dfp: DockerfileParser) -> list[str]:
+    return [s["value"] for s in dfp.structure if s["instruction"] == "COPY"]
+
+
+def describe_dockerfile_parity():
+    devcontainer = DockerfileParser(path=str(DEVCONTAINER_DOCKERFILE))
+    packaged = DockerfileParser(path=str(PACKAGED_DOCKERFILE))
+
+    def it_pins_the_same_playwright_base_image_version():
+        # devcontainer hardcodes the tag (the "Update Base Image Digest"
+        # workflow may append an `@sha256:...` pin to it); packaged
+        # parameterizes it via PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION so the same ARG can also pin
+        # the global playwright CLI installed later in that file. Compare the
+        # version, not the full image reference, so a digest pin on one side
+        # doesn't fail this check.
+        version_re = re.compile(r"playwright:v([\d.]+)-noble")
+        devcontainer_match = version_re.search(devcontainer.baseimage)
+        packaged_match = version_re.search(packaged.baseimage)
+        assert devcontainer_match, f"no playwright version found in {devcontainer.baseimage!r}"
+        assert packaged_match, f"no playwright version found in {packaged.baseimage!r}"
+        assert devcontainer_match.group(1) == packaged_match.group(1)
+
+    def it_shares_the_same_tool_version_pins():
+        for name in SHARED_ARG_DEFAULTS:
+            assert devcontainer.args[name] == packaged.args[name], name
+
+    def it_shares_the_same_run_instructions_for_common_setup():
+        for needle in SHARED_RUN_NEEDLES:
+            assert _run_containing(devcontainer, needle) == _run_containing(packaged, needle), needle
+
+    def it_copies_the_same_firewall_scripts_and_uv():
+        assert _copy_instructions(devcontainer) == _copy_instructions(packaged)
+
+    def it_shares_the_same_environment_block():
+        assert devcontainer.envs == packaged.envs

fix: lint both cage Dockerfiles and pin their shared invariants (#115)

* fix: lint both cage Dockerfiles and pin their shared invariants

hadolint only ever ran against .devcontainer/Dockerfile, so the packaged
Dockerfile shipped in the wheel (src/lamp_the_djinn/devcontainer/Dockerfile)
was never linted -- and its ignore config (.devcontainer/.hadolint.yaml)
was silently unused too, since hadolint only auto-discovers .hadolint.yaml
from the process cwd, not relative to the file being linted. Move the
config to the repo root so it covers both files, and lint both in CI.

Flip the job from advisory to blocking: fix the real DL4006 finding (add
a pipefail SHELL directive) on both files instead of adding it to the
ignore list, and fix an accidental drift found along the way (known_hosts
chmod 644 vs 600, no rationale for the weaker one).

Add an integration test pinning the invariants the two files must share
(base image version, tool version pins, the shared RUN/COPY/ENV
instructions) without asserting byte equality, since Docker CLI, the
pinned global Playwright CLI, and OCI labels are deliberately specific
to one image or the other.

Fixes #88

* e2e attestation for fix/dockerfile-parity-and-hadolint

+"""
+Integration tests pinning the shared invariants between the two cage Dockerfiles.
+
+`.devcontainer/Dockerfile` is what CI builds and publishes to ghcr.io -- the
+image `ltd` pulls by default. `src/lamp_the_djinn/devcontainer/Dockerfile` is
+the copy embedded in the wheel, used as the local-build fallback when the pull
+fails or `--build` is passed. Both run arbitrary agent workloads, so the tool
+versions and base image they hand an agent must not drift apart by accident.
+
+They also legitimately differ: only the packaged copy installs the Docker CLI
+and a pinned global Playwright CLI (a devcontainer.json used purely to develop
+this repo mounts no docker socket and needs neither), and only the published
+image carries OCI build-metadata labels. This test does not assert byte
+equality -- see the comments on each check for what is and isn't shared.
+
+The real, controlled collaborator is the host filesystem: dockerfile_parse
+reads the two files as they exist in this checkout. Nothing first-party is
+mocked.
+"""
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+from dockerfile_parse import DockerfileParser
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+DEVCONTAINER_DOCKERFILE = REPO_ROOT / ".devcontainer" / "Dockerfile"
+PACKAGED_DOCKERFILE = REPO_ROOT / "src" / "lamp_the_djinn" / "devcontainer" / "Dockerfile"
+
+# Bumping one of these in only one image is exactly the drift this test exists
+# to catch (see issue #88: PRs #79 and #85 each had to hand-patch both files).
+SHARED_ARG_DEFAULTS = ("CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION", "PI_VERSION", "GIT_DELTA_VERSION", "PNPM_VERSION")
+
+# RUN instructions that must be byte-identical between the two images,
+# identified by a substring unique to each.
+SHARED_RUN_NEEDLES = (
+    "apt-get install",
+    "pnpm@",
+    "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@",
+    "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@",
+    "known_hosts",
+)
+
+
+def _run_containing(dfp: DockerfileParser, needle: str) -> str:
+    matches = [s["value"] for s in dfp.structure if s["instruction"] == "RUN" and needle in s["value"]]
+    assert len(matches) == 1, f"expected exactly one RUN instruction containing {needle!r}, found {len(matches)}"
+    return matches[0]
+
+
+def _copy_instructions(dfp: DockerfileParser) -> list[str]:
+    return [s["value"] for s in dfp.structure if s["instruction"] == "COPY"]
+
+
+def describe_dockerfile_parity():
+    devcontainer = DockerfileParser(path=str(DEVCONTAINER_DOCKERFILE))
+    packaged = DockerfileParser(path=str(PACKAGED_DOCKERFILE))
+
+    def it_pins_the_same_playwright_base_image_version():
+        # devcontainer hardcodes the tag (the "Update Base Image Digest"
+        # workflow may append an `@sha256:...` pin to it); packaged

+        # the global playwright CLI installed later in that file. Compare the
+        # version, not the full image reference, so a digest pin on one side
+        # doesn't fail this check.
+        version_re = re.compile(r"playwright:v([\d.]+)-noble")
+        devcontainer_match = version_re.search(devcontainer.baseimage)
+        packaged_match = version_re.search(packaged.baseimage)
+        assert devcontainer_match, f"no playwright version found in {devcontainer.baseimage!r}"
+        assert packaged_match, f"no playwright version found in {packaged.baseimage!r}"
+        assert devcontainer_match.group(1) == packaged_match.group(1)
+
+    def it_shares_the_same_tool_version_pins():
+        for name in SHARED_ARG_DEFAULTS:
+            assert devcontainer.args[name] == packaged.args[name], name
+
+    def it_shares_the_same_run_instructions_for_common_setup():
+        for needle in SHARED_RUN_NEEDLES:
+            assert _run_containing(devcontainer, needle) == _run_containing(packaged, needle), needle
+
+    def it_copies_the_same_firewall_scripts_and_uv():
+        assert _copy_instructions(devcontainer) == _copy_instructions(packaged)
+
+    def it_shares_the_same_environment_block():
+        assert devcontainer.envs == packaged.envs

name: Testing Conventions

# Enforce the testing-conventions standard on this repo. Calls the upstream
# reusable workflow, which runs each rule as its own job -- so a failure names
# the rule that failed instead of collapsing every gate into one red step.
#   https://github.com/thekevinscott/testing-conventions
#
# This repo previously hand-rolled the same checks as a sequence of `npx` steps
# in a single job. That drifted: `one-function-per-file` and `mutation` were
# never wired up at all, and the version pin silently resolved a binary 34
# releases old. The reusable workflow runs every applicable gate by default, so
# a new rule arrives with an upstream release rather than waiting for someone
# to notice it is missing.
#
# Pinned to the upstream rolling `v0` tag, the same convention release.yml uses
# for putitoutthere: v0 tracks the latest backwards-compatible release.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'tests/**'
      - 'pyproject.toml'
      - 'testing-conventions.toml'
      - 'e2e-attestations/**'
      - '.github/workflows/conventions.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'tests/**'
      - 'pyproject.toml'
      - 'testing-conventions.toml'
      - 'e2e-attestations/**'
      - '.github/workflows/conventions.yml'

  mutation:

    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"mutation"')) && (needs.detect.outputs.mutation_languages || needs.detect.outputs.coverage_languages) != '[]' }}

      - if: matrix.language == 'rust'
        name: Cache the provisioned cargo-mutants

  e2e-verify:
    name: E2E attestation freshness (e2e verify)

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          # `--base` diffs `<base>..HEAD`, so full history is needed and `inputs.base` must resolve.
          # Check out the PR's head commit, not the ephemeral merge commit, which an attestation
          # can never name — it is rebuilt on every push.

          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

        with:

    name: Packaging (no test files in the built artifact)

          name: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact }}
          path: _packaging_artifact
      - name: Download the CLI built from HEAD (hermetic)
        if: needs.detect.outputs.cli_command != ''
        uses: ./.github/actions/download-hermetic-cli
      # cargo must be on PATH first: `cargo package` needs it, and `uv build`/`prepack` may compile a Rust core.
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' && (needs.detect.outputs.packaging_language == 'rust' || inputs.rust_toolchain || needs.detect.outputs.provision_rust == 'true') }}
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' && (needs.detect.outputs.packaging_language == 'rust' || inputs.rust_toolchain || needs.detect.outputs.provision_rust == 'true') }}
        name: Cache the Rust build (cargo registry + target)
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cargo_target_dir || format('{0}/target', needs.detect.outputs.package_root) }}
          key: rust-toolchain-build-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            rust-toolchain-build-${{ runner.os }}-
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_language == 'python' }}
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_language == 'typescript' && (needs.detect.outputs.ts_package_manager || 'pnpm') == 'pnpm' }}
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v5
        with:
          version: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.ts_pnpm_version || '>=11' }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_language == 'typescript' }}
        name: Install project dependencies
        working-directory: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
        env:
          PM: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.ts_package_manager || 'pnpm' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$PM" = "pnpm" ]; then pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; else npm ci; fi
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' && needs.detect.outputs.build_command != '' }}
        name: Run the build step (build_command)
        working-directory: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
        env:
          BUILD_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.build_command }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          eval "$BUILD_COMMAND"
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' }}
        name: Build the distribution (packaging_build)
        working-directory: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
        env:
          PACKAGING_BUILD: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          eval "$PACKAGING_BUILD"
      - name: Check the built distributions ship no test files
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          PACKAGING_ARTIFACT: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact }}
          PACKAGE_ROOT: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # nullglob: an unmatched glob expands to nothing, not the literal; globstar: `**` recurses.
          shopt -s nullglob globstar
          pkg="${PACKAGE_ROOT:-.}"
          if [ -n "$PACKAGING_ARTIFACT" ]; then dist_root=_packaging_artifact; crate_root=_packaging_artifact; else dist_root="$pkg/dist"; crate_root="$pkg/target/package"; fi
          checked=0
          check () {
            local lang="$1"; shift
            for dist in "$@"; do
              echo "::group::packaging --language $lang $dist"
              ${CLI_COMMAND:-npm --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP" exec --yes -- "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} packaging "$dist" --language "$lang"
              echo "::endgroup::"
              checked=$((checked + 1))
            done
          }
          check python "$dist_root"/**/*.whl "$dist_root"/**/*.tar.gz
          check typescript "$dist_root"/**/*.tgz
          check rust "$crate_root"/**/*.crate
          if [ "$checked" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::no recognized built distribution (.whl / .tar.gz / .tgz / .crate) found in '$dist_root' or '$crate_root'"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "checked $checked built distribution(s); no test files shipped"

  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: docs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v5
        with:
          version: 10.33.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist

  deploy:
    name: Deploy
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

name: Lint Dockerfile

# Scoped out of the old `Lint` workflow. See #102.
#
# Lints both cage Dockerfiles: .devcontainer/Dockerfile (what CI builds and
# publishes) and src/lamp_the_djinn/devcontainer/Dockerfile (the packaged
# local-build fallback). See #88/#103.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '.devcontainer/Dockerfile'
      - 'src/lamp_the_djinn/devcontainer/Dockerfile'
      - '.hadolint.yaml'
      - '.github/workflows/lint-dockerfile.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '.devcontainer/Dockerfile'
      - 'src/lamp_the_djinn/devcontainer/Dockerfile'
      - '.hadolint.yaml'
      - '.github/workflows/lint-dockerfile.yml'

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  hadolint:
    name: Hadolint (Dockerfiles)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download hadolint
        run: |
          curl -sL -o hadolint "https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint/releases/download/v2.12.0/hadolint-Linux-x86_64"
          chmod +x hadolint

      # Ignored rules, from .hadolint.yaml (auto-discovered from the repo
      # root, so it covers both files below without a --config flag):
      # DL3008: Pin versions in apt-get - not practical for either image
      # DL3059: Multiple consecutive RUN - intentional for caching
      # This job blocks the PR on any other finding -- see #103 for why it
      # used to run with continue-on-error and why that changed.
      - name: Run Hadolint on the devcontainer Dockerfile
        run: ./hadolint .devcontainer/Dockerfile

      - name: Run Hadolint on the packaged cage Dockerfile
        run: ./hadolint src/lamp_the_djinn/devcontainer/Dockerfile

name: Lint Python

# Split out of the old single `Lint` workflow, which had no `paths:` and so ran
# ruff, mypy, shellcheck and hadolint on every PR -- a Dockerfile edit ran mypy,
# a src/ edit ran hadolint. Paths filters are per-workflow, not per-job, so each
# tool needs its own file to be scoped. See #102.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '**/*.py'
      # ruff and mypy are both configured under [tool.*] here, so a config edit
      # changes the verdict without touching a single .py file.
      - 'pyproject.toml'
      - '.github/workflows/lint-python.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '**/*.py'
      - 'pyproject.toml'
      - '.github/workflows/lint-python.yml'

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  python:
    name: Python (ruff + mypy)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5

      - name: Ruff lint
        run: uvx ruff check .

      - name: Ruff format check
        run: uvx ruff format --check .

      - name: Mypy
        run: uvx mypy src/lamp_the_djinn

name: Lint Shell

# Scoped out of the old `Lint` workflow. See #102.
#
# The glob is repo-wide on purpose: shellcheck walks `find . -name '*.sh'`, and
# scripts live in six directories (scripts/, .devcontainer/, deploy/, fly/,
# grafana/, src/lamp_the_djinn/devcontainer/). Enumerating them would drift.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '**/*.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/lint-shell.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '**/*.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/lint-shell.yml'

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  shellcheck:
    name: ShellCheck
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install ShellCheck
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y shellcheck

      - name: Run ShellCheck
        run: |
          find . -name '*.sh' -type f | xargs shellcheck --severity=warning

name: Build and Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - '.devcontainer/**'
      - '.github/workflows/publish-cage-image.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - '.devcontainer/**'
      - '.github/workflows/publish-cage-image.yml'
  schedule:
    # Weekly on Sunday at midnight UTC - keeps GitHub Actions cache warm
    - cron: '0 0 * * 0'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      claude_code_version:
        description: 'Claude Code version to install'
        required: false
        default: 'latest'

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: linux/amd64
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - platform: linux/arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up QEMU (for cross-platform builds)
        if: matrix.platform != 'linux/arm64' || matrix.runner != 'ubuntu-24.04-arm'
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Log in to Container Registry
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Extract platform name
        id: platform
        run: echo "name=${PLATFORM//\//-}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        env:
          PLATFORM: ${{ matrix.platform }}

      - name: Extract metadata (tags, labels)
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}

      - name: Calculate Dockerfile hash
        id: dockerfile-hash
        run: echo "hash=$(sha256sum .devcontainer/Dockerfile | cut -c1-8)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Get build timestamp
        id: timestamp
        run: echo "value=$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Build and push by digest
        id: build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .devcontainer
          file: .devcontainer/Dockerfile
          platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          build-args: |
            CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=${{ inputs.claude_code_version || 'latest' }}
            BUILD_TIMESTAMP=${{ steps.timestamp.outputs.value }}
            BUILD_SOURCE=ghcr.io
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=${{ steps.platform.outputs.name }}-${{ steps.dockerfile-hash.outputs.hash }}
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=${{ steps.platform.outputs.name }}-${{ steps.dockerfile-hash.outputs.hash }}
          outputs: type=image,name=${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}

      - name: Export digest
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          mkdir -p /tmp/digests
          digest="${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}"
          touch "/tmp/digests/${digest#sha256:}"

      - name: Upload digest
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: digests-${{ steps.platform.outputs.name }}
          path: /tmp/digests/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  merge:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    needs: build
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    steps:
      - name: Download digests
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: /tmp/digests
          pattern: digests-*
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Log in to Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Extract metadata (tags, labels)
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}
            type=sha,prefix=

      - name: Create manifest list and push
        working-directory: /tmp/digests
        run: |
          docker buildx imagetools create $(jq -cr '.tags | map("-t " + .) | join(" ")' <<< "$DOCKER_METADATA_OUTPUT_JSON") \
            $(printf '${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}@sha256:%s ' *)

      - name: Inspect image
        run: |
          docker buildx imagetools inspect ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest

name: Release


on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  release:
    uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write

  # PyPI upload runs in the caller's workflow context: PyPI Trusted Publishers
  # can't validate OIDC tokens minted from a cross-repo reusable workflow.
  # The `if:` gate skips this job when the release job published nothing.
  pypi-publish:
    needs: release
    if: needs.release.outputs.has_pypi == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-sdist'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-wheel-*'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1

name: Test CLI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'tests/**'
      # Deps this lane installs via `uv sync`, plus [tool.pytest.ini_options]
      # (the unit/integration marker config both jobs select on).
      - 'pyproject.toml'
      - '.github/workflows/test-cli.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'tests/**'
      - 'pyproject.toml'
      - '.github/workflows/test-cli.yml'

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v4

      - name: Install project + dev dependencies
        run: uv sync --python 3.12

      - name: Run unit tests
        # Unit tier: colocated next to source (src/**/*_test.py), marked `unit`.
        run: uv run pytest src -m unit

  integration-tests:
    name: Integration Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v4

      - name: Install project + dev dependencies
        run: uv sync --python 3.12

      - name: Run integration tests
        # Integration tier (tests/integration), marked `integration`: first-party
        # code runs for real against the host filesystem/env; collaborators
        # (Docker, subprocess, network) are mocked, so no container is needed.
        run: uv run pytest tests/integration -m integration

name: Test Container

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - '.devcontainer/**'
      - '.github/workflows/test-container.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - '.devcontainer/**'
      - '.github/workflows/test-container.yml'

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Build test image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .devcontainer
          file: .devcontainer/Dockerfile
          load: true
          tags: lamp-the-djinn-test:latest

      - name: Test - uv is installed
        run: docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest uv --version

      - name: Test - uvx is installed
        run: docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest uvx --version

      - name: Test - pnpm is installed
        run: docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest pnpm --version

      - name: Test - npm is installed
        run: docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest npm --version

      - name: Test - node is installed
        run: docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest node --version

      - name: Test - claude is installed
        run: docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest claude --version

      - name: Test - git is installed
        run: docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest git --version

      - name: Test - firewall scripts exist
        run: |
          docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest ls -la /usr/local/bin/init-firewall.sh
          docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest ls -la /usr/local/bin/add-domain-to-firewall.sh
          docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest ls -la /usr/local/bin/safe-rm

      - name: Test - GPG setup script exists
        run: docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest ls -la /usr/local/bin/setup-gpg.sh

      - name: Test - whitelisted domains file exists
        run: docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest cat /usr/local/share/whitelisted-domains.txt | head -20

      - name: Test - runs as non-root user
        run: |
          USER=$(docker run --rm lamp-the-djinn-test:latest whoami)
          if [ "$USER" != "node" ]; then
            echo "Expected user 'node', got '$USER'"
            exit 1
          fi
